I've been working this land for 35 years. I know how Quzhou's soil behaves, I know the rains, I know when to water from the well. My back isn't what it was, but I know what I'm doing.

My main income is wheat and maize — that rotation has fed my family for decades. I'll keep roughly 8 mu on that rotation. The rest I split between cotton and garlic. Cotton brings cash but it's hard work; at my age I'll keep it to about 4 mu. Garlic I grow on about 4 mu — it sells well at market in May when it's ready.

For wheat, I'll plant the improved local variety everyone here uses — higher yield, good resistance. I always do rotary tillage after maize harvest in October, then sow. I water three times: once before sowing to get moisture in, once at jointing in March, once at heading in April. I apply urea and diammonium phosphate as base fertilizer, then top-dress nitrogen at jointing. Two spray rounds for aphids and powdery mildew.

For summer maize, I go straight in after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste. I use hybrid seed, the kind the supply cooperative sells. I broadcast fertilizer and water twice unless there's decent rain.

Cotton I'll plough deeper — cotton likes loose soil. I use BT hybrid cotton seed so I don't have to spray as much for bollworm, but I still spray 5 times for other pests and disease. Water 4 times through summer.

Garlic I plant in October after the maize ground is cleared on that plot. I use my own saved cloves from last year — good quality, no need to buy. Garlic needs water often, especially in spring when the bulbs are swelling.
